name: Angau

facts.text: Welsh: angau means 'death' (to verify against a dictionary).
Angau as a soldier who would not be buried, and the worms that will not leave him, are Living Server writing.

story:
The hill-folk of the Pennines call him Angau, which is their old word for death, and they do not mean it as a name. They mean it as a warning. He is a soldier, or was, in a harness of a pattern older than any of the caers, and he stands on the northern tops in a hollow full of worms.

The story the riders tell is that he would not be buried. His company fell on the tops in some war before the caers were built, and the others went into the ground as soldiers do, and he got up out of his grave and stood in it, and said he had not been relieved. The worms came for him as worms do, and could not finish him, and have stayed, as if they were waiting their turn. They are still waiting. The riders say Angau has outlasted three generations of the worms.

Corporal Dilys's book of the tops gives him a line of his own: 'Angau. Do not stop. Do not answer.' The riders have added, in different hands, under it: 'He does not ask anything.' 'He does not need to.'
legend: Angau, level 40 ghost legionnaire, on the northern Pennine tops in a hollow with a handful of worms (40). The worms are not his faction but they are right there and aggressive, so clear them first. Plain melee, no spells; crush for the bones. A group around forty handles it. Respawn ten minutes. The riders' advice: do not stop near him.

slay: The worms will have you instead.
